sanskrit: vane mūlaphalāśī ca tapyan suvipulaṃ tapaḥ puṇyāyatanacārī ca bhūtānām avihiṃsakaḥ
english: In the forest, living on roots and fruits, mortifying himself with austerity most vast, ranging among holy sanctuaries and doing no harm to any living being—

sanskrit: vidhūme sannamusale vānaprasthapratiśraye kāle prāpte caran bhaikṣaṃ kalpate brahmabhūyase
english: When the smoke has cleared and the pestle is laid to rest, dwelling in the hermitage of the forest-recluse, going forth to beg at the appointed hour—such a man grows fit for union with Brahman.

sanskrit: niḥstutir nirnamaskāraḥ parityajya śubhāśubhe araṇye vicaraikākī yena kena cid āśitaḥ
english: Free of praise, free of obeisance, having cast off the good and the ill alike, let him wander alone in the wilderness, sustained by whatever may come.

sanskrit: śuka uvāca yad idaṃ vedavacanaṃ lokavāde virudhyate pramāṇe cāpramāṇe ca viruddhe śāstratā kutaḥ
english: Śuka said: When this pronouncement of the Veda stands at odds with the speech of the world, and authority and non-authority are thus in conflict, where then is the standing of scripture?

sanskrit: ity etac chrotum icchāmi bhagavān prabravītu me karmaṇām avirodhena katham etat pravartate
english: This I wish to hear; let the venerable one expound it to me: how does this proceed without contradicting the path of works?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity uktaḥ pratyuvācedaṃ gandhavatyāḥ sutaḥ sutam ṛṣis tat pūjayan vākyaṃ putrasyāmitatejasaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed, the son of Gandhavatī answered his son, the sage honoring the question of that boy of measureless splendor.

sanskrit: gṛhastho brahmacārī ca vānaprastho 'tha bhikṣukaḥ yathoktakāriṇaḥ sarve gacchanti paramāṃ gatim
english: The householder, the student, the forest-recluse, and the mendicant—all of them, if they do as is enjoined, reach the supreme goal.

sanskrit: eko ya āśramān etān anutiṣṭhed yathāvidhi akāmadveṣasaṃyuktaḥ sa paratra mahīyate
english: He who alone observes these stages of life one by one, each according to its rule, joined neither to desire nor to hatred, is exalted in the world beyond.

sanskrit: catuṣpadī hi niḥśreṇī brahmaṇy eṣā pratiṣṭhitā etām āśritya niḥśreṇīṃ brahmaloke mahīyate
english: For this is a four-runged ladder, set firm upon Brahman; resting upon this ladder, a man is exalted in the world of Brahman.

sanskrit: āyuṣas tu caturbhāgaṃ brahmacāryanasūyakaḥ gurau vā guruputre vā vased dharmārthakovidaḥ
english: A quarter of his life let the student dwell, free of envy and skilled in dharma and its purpose, with his teacher or with his teacher's son.

sanskrit: karmātirekeṇa guror adhyetavyaṃ bubhūṣatā dakṣiṇo nāpavādī syād āhūto gurum āśrayet
english: He who would prosper must study, going beyond mere duty for his teacher's sake; let him be deft and never given to reproach, and attend his teacher when summoned.

sanskrit: jaghanyaśāyī pūrvaṃ syād utthāyī guruveśmani yac ca śiṣyeṇa kartavyaṃ kāryaṃ dāsena vā punaḥ
english: In the teacher's house let him be the last to lie down and the first to rise; and whatever ought to be done by a pupil, or again by a servant—

sanskrit: kṛtam ity eva tat sarvaṃ kṛtvā tiṣṭheta pārśvataḥ kiṃkaraḥ sarvakārī ca sarvakarmasu kovidaḥ
english: all of that, regarding it as simply his to do, let him perform, and then stand ready at his teacher's side—a willing servant, doing all things, skilled in every task.

sanskrit: śucir dakṣo guṇopeto brūyād iṣur ivātvaraḥ cakṣuṣā gurum avyagro nirīkṣeta jitendriyaḥ
english: Pure, capable, endowed with virtue, let him speak straight as an arrow yet unhurried; with his senses mastered and his mind composed, let him look upon his teacher with steady gaze.

sanskrit: nābhuktavati cāśnīyād apītavati no pibet na tiṣṭhati tathāsīta nāsupte prasvapeta ca
english: While the teacher has not eaten, let him not eat; while the teacher has not drunk, let him not drink; while the teacher stands, let him not sit; while the teacher is awake, let him not sleep.

sanskrit: uttānābhyāṃ ca pāṇibhyāṃ pādāv asya mṛdu spṛśet dakṣiṇaṃ dakṣiṇenaiva savyaṃ savyena pīḍayet
english: With both hands upturned let him gently touch his teacher's feet—the right foot with the right hand, the left foot pressing with the left.

sanskrit: abhivādya guruṃ brūyād adhīṣva bhagavann iti idaṃ kariṣye bhagavann idaṃ cāpi kṛtaṃ mayā
english: Having saluted the teacher, let him say, "Teach, O venerable one"; "This I shall do, O venerable one"; and "This, too, has been done by me."

sanskrit: iti sarvam anujñāpya nivedya gurave dhanam kuryāt kṛtvā ca tat sarvam ākhyeyaṃ gurave punaḥ
english: Thus seeking leave for everything and laying his earnings before the teacher, let him act; and having acted, let him report all of it to the teacher again.

sanskrit: yāṃs tu gandhān rasān vāpi brahmacārī na sevate seveta tān samāvṛtta iti dharmeṣu niścayaḥ
english: Whatever scents or savors the student forgoes, these he may enjoy once he has returned from his studies—such is the settled rule in matters of dharma.

sanskrit: ye ke cid vistareṇoktā niyamā brahmacāriṇaḥ tān sarvān anugṛhṇīyād bhavec cānapago guroḥ
english: Whatever restraints have been laid down at length for the student, let him take them all upon himself, and let him not stray from his teacher.

sanskrit: sa evaṃ gurave prītim upahṛtya yathābalam āśrameṣv āśrameṣv evaṃ śiṣyo varteta karmaṇā
english: Thus offering his teacher devotion to the best of his power, the pupil should so conduct himself by his works in stage after stage of life.

sanskrit: vedavratopavāsena caturthe cāyuṣo gate gurave dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā samāvarted yathāvidhi
english: When through study of the Veda, his vows, and his fasting the first quarter of life has passed, let him give the teacher his fee and return home as the rule prescribes.

sanskrit: dharmalabdhair yuto dārair agnīn utpādya dharmataḥ dvitīyam āyuṣo bhāgaṃ gṛhamedhivratī bhavet
english: United with a wife won by righteous means and kindling the sacred fires according to dharma, let him for the second quarter of life take up the vow of the householder.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca dvitīyam āyuṣo bhāgaṃ gṛhamedhī gṛhe vaset dharmalabdhair yuto dārair agnīn utpādya suvrataḥ
english: Vyāsa said: For the second quarter of life let the householder dwell at home, united with a wife won by righteous means and, true to his vows, having kindled the sacred fires.

sanskrit: gṛhasthavṛttayaś caiva catasraḥ kavibhiḥ smṛtāḥ kusūladhānyaḥ prathamaḥ kumbhīdhānyas tv anantaram
english: Four modes of livelihood for the householder are recorded by the wise: the first is he who stores grain in a granary, then he who stores it in a jar,

sanskrit: aśvastano 'tha kāpotīm āśrito vṛttim āharet teṣāṃ paraḥ paro jyāyān dharmato lokajittamaḥ
english: then he who keeps no store for the morrow, and then he who gathers his living dove-like, grain by fallen grain; of these, each later one is the higher, and by dharma the best winner of worlds.

sanskrit: ṣaṭkarmā vartayaty ekas tribhir anyaḥ pravartate dvābhyām ekaś caturthas tu brahmasatre vyavasthitaḥ gṛhamedhivratāny atra mahāntīha pracakṣate
english: One lives by the six occupations, another conducts himself by three, one by two, while the fourth is established in the sacrificial session of Brahman; mighty, they declare, are the householder's vows herein.

sanskrit: nātmārthaṃ pācayed annaṃ na vṛthā ghātayet paśūn prāṇī vā yadi vāprāṇī saṃskāraṃ yajuṣārhati
english: He should not cook food for himself alone, nor needlessly slay beasts; whatever, living or lifeless, is fit to be consecrated with the sacrificial formula—that he should so hallow.

sanskrit: na divā prasvapej jātu na pūrvāpararātrayoḥ na bhuñjītāntarākāle nānṛtāv āhvayet striyam
english: Let him never sleep by day, nor in the first or last watches of the night; let him not eat between the proper times, nor approach his wife out of season.

sanskrit: nāsyānaśnan vased vipro gṛhe kaś cid apūjitaḥ tathāsyātithayaḥ pūjyā havyakavyavahāḥ sadā
english: Let no brāhmaṇa dwell unfed and unhonored in his house; and his guests, the bearers of offerings to gods and ancestors, are ever to be revered.

sanskrit: vedavidyāvratasnātāḥ śrotriyā vedapāragāḥ svadharmajīvino dāntāḥ kriyāvantas tapasvinaḥ teṣāṃ havyaṃ ca kavyaṃ cāpy arhaṇārthaṃ vidhīyate
english: Those bathed in the lore and vows of the Veda, learned in sacred recitation and versed to the end of the Veda, who live by their own dharma, self-controlled, active in rite and rich in austerity—to them the offerings for gods and ancestors are ordained as their due honor.

sanskrit: na kharaiḥ saṃprayātasya svadharmājñānakasya ca apaviddhāgnihotrasya guror vālīkakāriṇaḥ
english: But not so for the man gone wandering with asses, ignorant of his own dharma, one who has cast aside the fire-offering, or who deals falsely with his teacher.

sanskrit: saṃvibhāgo 'tra bhūtānāṃ sarveṣām eva śiṣyate tathaivāpacamānebhyaḥ pradeyaṃ gṛhamedhinā
english: Herein a fair share is enjoined for all living beings, and likewise the householder should give to those who do not cook for themselves.

sanskrit: vighasāśī bhaven nityaṃ nityaṃ cāmṛtabhojanaḥ amṛtaṃ yajñaśeṣaṃ syād bhojanaṃ haviṣā samam bhṛtyaśeṣaṃ tu yo 'śnāti tam āhur vighasāśinam
english: Let him ever eat the leavings of others and ever feed on what is like nectar; the remnant of the sacrifice is that nectar, food as sacred as the oblation, and he who eats what is left after his dependents have eaten is called the eater of leavings.

sanskrit: svadāranirato dānto hy anasūyur jitendriyaḥ ṛtvikpurohitācāryair mātulātithisaṃśritaiḥ
english: Devoted to his own wife, self-restrained, free of malice, his senses mastered—with the officiating priests, the family priest, and the teachers, with maternal uncles and the guests who shelter with him,

sanskrit: vṛddhabālāturair vaidyair jñātisaṃbandhibāndhavaiḥ mātāpitṛbhyāṃ jāmībhir bhrātrā putreṇa bhāryayā
english: with the aged, the young, the sick, with physicians, kinsmen, relations by marriage, and friends, with mother and father, with sisters, with brother, son, and wife,

sanskrit: duhitrā dāsavargeṇa vivādaṃ na samācaret etān vimucya saṃvādān sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: with daughter and with the band of servants—let him engage in no quarrel; renouncing such disputes, he is freed from all sins.

sanskrit: etair jitais tu jayati sarvāṃl lokān na saṃśayaḥ ācāryo brahmalokeśaḥ prājāpatye pitā prabhuḥ
english: By overcoming these contentions he wins, beyond doubt, all the worlds; the teacher is lord of Brahman's world, the father master of the realm of Prajāpati,

sanskrit: atithis tv indralokeśo devalokasya cartvijaḥ jāmayo 'psarasāṃ loke vaiśvadeve tu jñātayaḥ
english: the guest is lord of Indra's world, the officiating priests of the world of the gods; sisters belong in the world of the apsarases, and kinsmen in the realm of the Viśvedevas.

sanskrit: saṃbandhibāndhavā dikṣu pṛthivyāṃ mātṛmātulau vṛddhabālāturakṛśās tv ākāśe prabhaviṣṇavaḥ
english: Relations by marriage and friends rule in the quarters of space, mother and maternal uncle upon the earth; the aged, the young, the sick, and the frail hold sway in the sky.

sanskrit: bhrātā jyeṣṭhaḥ samaḥ pitrā bhāryā putraḥ svakā tanuḥ chāyā svā dāśavargas tu duhitā kṛpaṇaṃ param
english: An elder brother is the equal of a father; wife and son are one's own body; the band of servants is one's own shadow; and a daughter is the highest object of one's tenderness.

sanskrit: tasmād etair adhikṣiptaḥ sahen nityam asaṃjvaraḥ gṛhadharmarato vidvān dharmanityo jitaklamaḥ
english: Therefore, though provoked by these, let the wise man ever endure it without fever of resentment—devoted to the householder's dharma, constant in righteousness, master of his weariness.

sanskrit: na cārthabaddhaḥ karmāṇi dharmaṃ vā kaṃ cid ācaret gṛhasthavṛttayas tisras tāsāṃ niḥśreyasaṃ param
english: Nor, bound to wealth, should he perform any rite or any act of dharma for gain; of the three modes of the householder's life, the highest is the one that leads to release.

sanskrit: parasparaṃ tathaivāhuś cāturāśramyam eva tat ye coktā niyamās teṣāṃ sarvaṃ kāryaṃ bubhūṣatā
english: They say, too, that these stand in mutual relation: this very fourfold order of life's stages. Whatever restraints have been laid down for them, all must be fulfilled by him who would prosper.

sanskrit: kumbhīdhānyair uñchaśilaiḥ kāpotīṃ cāsthitais tathā yasmiṃś caite vasanty arhās tad rāṣṭram abhivardhate
english: That kingdom flourishes wherein dwell such worthy men—those who store grain in a jar, those who live by gleaning fallen ears, and those who hold to the dove-like way.

sanskrit: daśa pūrvān daśa parān punāti ca pitāmahān gṛhasthavṛttayas tv etā vartayed yo gatavyathaḥ
english: He purifies ten forebears and ten descendants who, free of distress, lives by these modes of the householder's life.

sanskrit: sa cakracaralokānāṃ sadṛśīṃ prāpnuyād gatim yatendriyāṇām atha vā gatir eṣā vidhīyate
english: He attains a goal like that of the dwellers in the wheeling spheres; this destiny is ordained for those whose senses are restrained.

sanskrit: svargaloko gṛhasthānām udāramanasāṃ hitaḥ svargo vimānasaṃyukto vedadṛṣṭaḥ supuṣpitaḥ
english: For householders of generous mind the world of heaven is appointed—heaven furnished with celestial cars, beheld in the Veda, in full and lovely flower.

sanskrit: svargaloke gṛhasthānāṃ pratiṣṭhā niyatātmanām brahmaṇā vihitā śreṇir eṣā yasmāt pramucyate dvitīyaṃ kramaśaḥ prāpya svargaloke mahīyate
english: In the world of heaven is the standing-place of householders who are masters of themselves; this rung was ordained by Brahman, and from it one is set free—having reached in due order the second stage, one is exalted in the world of heaven.

sanskrit: ataḥ paraṃ paramam udāram āśramaṃ; tṛtīyam āhus tyajatāṃ kalevaram vanaukasāṃ gṛhapatinām anuttamaṃ; śṛṇuṣvaitat kliṣṭaśarīrakāriṇām
english: Beyond this they declare a noble stage supreme—the third—for those who would forsake the body: matchless for the forest-dwellers who were once householders. Hear now of these who put their bodies to hardship.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca proktā gṛhasthavṛttis te vihitā yā manīṣiṇām tadanantaram uktaṃ yat tan nibodha yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: The householder's mode of life, as ordained for the wise, has been declared to you; mark now, Yudhiṣṭhira, what is taught as following thereupon.

sanskrit: kramaśas tv avadhūyaināṃ tṛtīyāṃ vṛttim uttamām saṃyogavratakhinnānāṃ vānaprasthāśramaukasām
english: Shaking off this stage in due order, hear of the third and higher mode of life—of those wearied by the vows of householding, who dwell in the hermitage of the forest-recluse,

sanskrit: śrūyatāṃ pārtha bhadraṃ te sarvalokāśrayātmanām prekṣāpūrvaṃ pravṛttānāṃ puṇyadeśanivāsinām
english: Listen, Pārtha—blessings upon you—of those whose souls are a refuge to all the worlds, who set forth with foresight and dwell in holy regions.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca gṛhasthas tu yadā paśyed valīpalitam ātmanaḥ apatyasyaiva cāpatyaṃ vanam eva tadāśrayet
english: Vyāsa said: When the householder sees his own wrinkles and gray hair, and the offspring of his offspring, then let him betake himself to the forest.

sanskrit: tṛtīyam āyuṣo bhāgaṃ vānaprasthāśrame vaset tān evāgnīn paricared yajamāno divaukasaḥ
english: For the third quarter of life let him dwell in the order of the forest-recluse, tending those same sacred fires and offering sacrifice to the dwellers in heaven.

sanskrit: niyato niyatāhāraḥ ṣaṣṭhabhakto 'pramādavān tad agnihotraṃ tā gāvo yajñāṅgāni ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Disciplined, of measured food, eating but at every sixth mealtime, and ever vigilant—his is that fire-offering, his those cattle, and his all the appurtenances of sacrifice.

sanskrit: akṛṣṭaṃ vai vrīhiyavaṃ nīvāraṃ vighasāni ca havīṃṣi saṃprayaccheta makheṣv atrāpi pañcasu
english: Rice and barley untilled, wild grain, and gleaned leavings—these he should offer as oblations in the five great sacrifices observed here.

sanskrit: vānaprasthāśrame 'py etāś catasro vṛttayaḥ smṛtāḥ sadyaḥprakṣālakāḥ ke cit ke cin māsikasaṃcayāḥ
english: In the order of the forest-recluse, too, four modes are recorded: some wash and consume their food the same day, some store enough for a month,

sanskrit: vārṣikaṃ saṃcayaṃ ke cit ke cid dvādaśavārṣikam kurvanty atithipūjārthaṃ yajñatantrārthasiddhaye
english: some lay up a year's store, and some a store of twelve years, doing so to honor guests and to accomplish the rites of sacrifice.

sanskrit: abhrāvakāśā varṣāsu hemante jalasaṃśrayāḥ grīṣme ca pañcatapasaḥ śaśvac ca mitabhojanāḥ
english: In the rains they take the open sky for shelter, in winter they resort to the waters, in summer they sit amid the five fires, and always they eat but sparingly.

sanskrit: bhūmau viparivartante tiṣṭhed vā prapadair api sthānāsanair vartayanti savaneṣv abhiṣiñcate
english: They roll upon the bare ground, or stand upon their toes; they pass their lives standing or seated, and bathe at the times of the three pressings.

sanskrit: dantolūkhalinaḥ ke cid aśmakuṭṭās tathāpare śuklapakṣe pibanty eke yavāgūṃ kvathitāṃ sakṛt
english: Some use their teeth for a mortar, others pound their food with stones; some, in the bright fortnight, drink boiled barley-gruel but once a day.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇapakṣe pibanty eke bhuñjate ca yathākramam mūlair eke phalair eke puṣpair eke dṛḍhavratāḥ
english: Some drink it in the dark fortnight and eat in due succession; some, firm in their vows, live on roots, some on fruits, some on flowers.

sanskrit: vartayanti yathānyāyaṃ vaikhānasamataṃ śritāḥ etāś cānyāś ca vividhā dīkṣās teṣāṃ manīṣiṇām
english: Holding to the doctrine of the Vaikhānasas, they live as the rule requires; these and many other diverse observances belong to those sages.

sanskrit: caturthaś caupaniṣado dharmaḥ sādhāraṇaḥ smṛtaḥ vānaprastho gṛhasthaś ca tato 'nyaḥ saṃpravartate
english: And the fourth, the dharma of the Upaniṣads, is held to be common to all; from it, beyond the forest-recluse and the householder alike, yet another way proceeds.

sanskrit: asminn eva yuge tāta vipraiḥ sarvārthadarśibhiḥ agastyaḥ sapta ṛṣayo madhucchando 'ghamarṣaṇaḥ
english: In this very age, my child, by brāhmaṇas who beheld all truths—Agastya, the Seven Seers, Madhucchandas, Aghamarṣaṇa,

sanskrit: sāṃkṛtiḥ sudivā taṇḍir yavānno 'tha kṛtaśramaḥ ahovīryas tathā kāvyas tāṇḍyo medhātithir budhaḥ
english: Sāṃkṛti, Sudivā, Taṇḍi, Yavānna, and Kṛtaśrama, Ahovīrya, Kāvya, Tāṇḍya, and the sage Medhātithi,

sanskrit: śalo vākaś ca nirvākaḥ śūnyapālaḥ kṛtaśramaḥ evaṃdharmasu vidvāṃsas tataḥ svargam upāgaman
english: Śala, Vāka and Nirvāka, Śūnyapāla and Kṛtaśrama—these, learned in such observances of dharma, thereupon ascended to heaven.

sanskrit: tāta pratyakṣadharmāṇas tathā yāyāvarā gaṇāḥ ṛṣīṇām ugratapasāṃ dharmanaipuṇadarśinām
english: My child, the bands of wandering seers whose righteousness was made manifest, sages of fierce austerity who beheld the fine subtleties of dharma—

sanskrit: avācyāparimeyāś ca brāhmaṇā vanam āśritāḥ vaikhānasā vālakhilyāḥ sikatāś ca tathāpare
english: brāhmaṇas beyond naming and beyond number who resorted to the forest, the Vaikhānasas, the Vālakhilyas, the Sikatās, and others still—

sanskrit: karmabhis te nirānandā dharmanityā jitendriyāḥ gatāḥ pratyakṣadharmāṇas te sarve vanam āśritāḥ anakṣatrā anādhṛṣyā dṛśyante jyotiṣāṃ gaṇāḥ
english: taking no delight in worldly works, constant in dharma, their senses subdued, all of them—their righteousness made manifest—betook themselves to the forest, and now, beyond the constellations and unassailable, they are seen as hosts of stars.

sanskrit: jarayā ca paridyūno vyādhinā ca prapīḍitaḥ caturthe cāyuṣaḥ śeṣe vānaprasthāśramaṃ tyajet sadyaskārāṃ nirūpyeṣṭiṃ sarvavedasadakṣiṇām
english: Worn down by age and afflicted by disease, in the fourth and last remnant of his life let him forsake the order of the forest-recluse, having performed the same-day rite with all his possessions for its priestly fee.

sanskrit: ātmayājī so ''tmaratir ātmakrīḍātmasaṃśrayaḥ ātmany agnīn samāropya tyaktvā sarvaparigrahān
english: Sacrificing to the Self, taking joy in the Self, sporting in the Self, resting upon the Self, he draws the sacred fires up into his own Self and casts off all possessions.

sanskrit: sadyaskrāṃś ca yajed yajñān iṣṭīś caiveha sarvadā sadaiva yājināṃ yajñād ātmanījyā nivartate
english: Let him offer same-day sacrifices and oblations here always; ever, from the outward rite of those who sacrifice, the worship turns back to the Self alone.

sanskrit: trīṃś caivāgnīn yajet samyag ātmany evātmamokṣaṇāt prāṇebhyo yajuṣā pañca ṣaṭ prāśnīyād akutsayan
english: And let him duly offer the three fires within the Self itself, for the sake of the Self's release; with the sacrificial formula he should make five offerings to the breaths, and eat six mouthfuls without disdain.

sanskrit: keśalomanakhān vāpya vānaprastho munis tataḥ āśramād āśramaṃ sadyaḥ pūto gacchati karmabhiḥ
english: Having shorn his hair, his bodily hair, and his nails, the forest-recluse, now a silent sage, passes purified by his works at once from one stage of life to the next.

sanskrit: abhayaṃ sarvabhūtebhyo yo dattvā pravrajed dvijaḥ lokās tejomayās tasya pretya cānantyam aśnute
english: The twice-born who, having granted freedom from fear to all living beings, goes forth to the wandering life—worlds of radiance are his, and after death he attains the endless.

sanskrit: suśīlavṛtto vyapanītakalmaṣo; na ceha nāmutra ca kartum īhate aroṣamoho gatasaṃdhivigraho; bhaved udāsīnavad ātmavin naraḥ
english: Of fair conduct and character, his stains washed away, he strives to act neither for this world nor the next; free of anger and delusion, beyond alliance and enmity, the man who knows the Self should abide as one wholly indifferent.

sanskrit: yameṣu caivātmagateṣu na vyathet; svaśāstrasūtrāhutimantravikramaḥ bhaved yatheṣṭā gatir ātmayājino; na saṃśayo dharmapare jītendriye
english: Let him not waver in the restraints that belong to the Self, his strength lying in his own scripture, sacred thread, oblation, and mantra; a path at will belongs to him who sacrifices to the Self—no doubt of it, for one devoted to dharma whose senses are mastered.

sanskrit: tataḥ paraṃ śreṣṭham atīva sadguṇair; adhiṣṭhitaṃ trīn adhivṛttam uttamam caturtham uktaṃ paramāśramaṃ śṛṇu; prakīrtyamānaṃ paramaṃ parāyaṇam
english: Beyond this, hear of that which is best, surpassing in noble virtues, established above and beyond the other three—the supreme: the fourth, the highest stage of life now declared, the loftiest refuge being proclaimed to you.
